intro: Listen to the quiet. You are in Soğanlı Valley, a rock settlement in Kayseri province from the 9th to the 13th century. This is the quiet valley of Cappadocia: dozens of churches are cut into its slopes, and their frescoes, unlike Göreme's, mostly stand without a crowd in front of them.
history: This valley in southern Cappadocia was a monastic district, settled by Byzantine monks between the ninth and thirteenth centuries. The dozens of churches cut into its slopes repeat, in domed and cross-plan form, what Göreme offers. The difference? Here their frescoes usually stand without anyone in front of them. The valley falls within the World Heritage inscription made with the Göreme National Park.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Domed Church and the Church of the Snake, step into the Karabaş Church and the Church of the Deer, and look up at the Dovecotes.
facts: Did you know? The dovecotes cut into the valley's rock were not decorative. For centuries, pigeon droppings were the main fertiliser of its vineyards and gardens. And although the valley falls within the same World Heritage inscription as the Göreme National Park, it sees only a fraction of its visitors.
outro: This brings our journey through Soğanlı Valley to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let the valley keep its quiet for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
